why: The export and home profits add to the stated totals each year (30-20=10, 30+0=30, 30-10=20, 40-10=30), and the 1-3% margins imply total sales of about 800-1,200 million, which is believable for a brewer.
50 cities taking $24bn of a $135bn lower-income market is plausible, and so is a top city near $6.6bn and a second near $3.5bn; the flat tail on the unlabelled chart is a reading.
A podcast network with about $140m revenue and 359 producers works out to roughly $0.2-0.5m per producer by category, which is believable.
Market shares of 0.2-8.4% in export markets are believable, and margins of 10-37% are high for farm machinery but within a factor of a few of what it could report.
Sales of 410-520 thousand tyres a year in national markets of 2.5-3.6 million give shares of about 15-17%, which is believable for a tyre maker.
Shares of 1-7% and margins of 9-42% are believable for pet food, and the implied Country 5 profit of about $20m on a $1.3bn market is reasonable.
Each hotel's purpose-of-stay split adds to 100%, and 365-470 guest nights per room per year fits per-person guest nights at normal occupancy with more than one guest in some rooms.
A loss-making car-sharing club growing from EUR 17m to EUR 114m revenue, with losses that narrow from 156% to 28% of revenue, is believable, since losses can exceed revenue.
About 1.3 million sales, technical and administrative staff in a catchment, split by company size and contact level, is believable for a large metropolitan area.
Corporate telecom contracts worth $1-12m a year, with switching probabilities of 20-50%, are believable for a bank, a hospital group, a logistics firm and a retailer.
